question.text: A spherical soap bubble of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is formed inside another spherical soap bubble of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. If the internal pressure of the smaller bubble of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> in the above system is equal to the internal pressure of the another single soap bubble of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math> is _____

solution.text:
Pressure inside a bubble is given by, P0+4Tr.

Pressure inside the bubble of smaller radius will be, 

P2-P1=P0+4T6+4T3

Pressure inside the bubble with radius r, P0+4Tr

Now,

⇒P0+4T6+4T3=P0+4Tr

⇒1r=16+13

⇒r=2 cm
